title: Graceful Adoption Fence for Optimize Autopilot
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a robust, operator-friendly "Graceful Adoption Fence" that allows Optimize to auto-apply batching and KV-cache recommendations while minimizing risk to latency, correctness, and customer SLAs. Scope includes: (1) a gated rollout engine that can express staged cohorts (fractional traffic, tenant blacklists, region tags), (2) policy-driven canaries with simulated-traffic and shadow-check phases, (3) approval/escrow flows for human-in-the-loop intervention, and (4) comprehensive rollback and post-mortem playbooks.

Design highlights and trade-offs: we favor a conservative default (small initial cohorts + strong telemetry gating) to avoid noisy regressions; this increases time-to-value for some recommendations but dramatically reduces customer-visible incidents. We will reuse the existing rollout primitives in the deployment-controller where possible, but introduce a lightweight recommendation sandbox to run simulated inference (prefix-preserving KV cache checks) before committing changes. Canary decisions will be based on a small number of SLO-focused signals (p50/p95 latency, token error rate, throughput, and a quality delta metric derived from sampled prompt evals).

Integration points: Redwood Console (rollout UI + approval task), Optimize suggestion engine (recommendation metadata), runtime (applyable config schema + fast revert API), and telemetry (new datadog/Grafana dashboards and a canary-specific tracing span).

Operator UX: an approval card in the Console with estimated cost savings, expected impact distribution, a simulated-preview button, and an "Escrow & Auto-Approve" toggle that requires Ops acknowledgment. Default behavior: staged auto-apply with an initial 2% cohort, automated health checks at 15/60/180 minutes, and automatic ramp to target only if all gates pass. Manual approval can accelerate ramps.

Rollback and incident playbook: immediate rollback on any safety gate breach (predefined thresholds), automated post-rollback data capture (trace + sample prompts), and a one-click revert that restores previous configs and triggers an incident runbook. We will also capture lessons into a template PRD for future policy tuning.

Success criteria: no customer-facing SLA breaches in first 30 staged rollouts, median rollout time reduced vs fully manual by 40%, and telemetry reliably surfacing false-positive quality regressions under 3% false alarm rate during simulated canaries.
